title: Veterans' Group Life Insurance (VGLI) Applications: Acceptance Windows and Initial Coverage
content:
# Veterans' Group Life Insurance (VGLI) Applications: Acceptance Windows and Initial Coverage

## Governing rule

A VGLI application is accepted without health questions only if it is received not later than 240 calendar days after the date SGLI coverage ended. Count calendar days starting the day after SGLI coverage ended; an application received on the last day qualifies. An application received after that but within 485 days must show good health, and a later application is not accepted. Initial coverage cannot exceed the SGLI coverage held at separation and is chosen in multiples of $10,000 between $10,000 and $500,000. Coverage begins when the first premium is received with the application.

This rule applies to every Veterans' Group Life Insurance (VGLI) coverage tier.

## The acceptance windows, condition by condition

| Element | What governs it |
|---|---|
| Starting point | the date SGLI coverage ended, as the system records it for the applicant |
| Counting | calendar days; day 1 is the day after SGLI coverage ended |
| Date tested | the date the application is received |
| No-health window | received not later than day 240; day 240 itself qualifies |
| Health-proof window | received after day 240 but within 485 days |
| After the windows | an application received later is not accepted |

The date SGLI coverage ended is taken from the system record for the same applicant whose application is being decided; the applicant's own account of when coverage ended does not replace that record. The test is made before the policy is issued.

The three rows "not later than day 240", "after that but within 485 days" and "later" cover every receipt date, and each receipt date falls in exactly one of them:

| Application received | Accepted? | Health questions |
|---|---|---|
| on or before day 240 | yes | none |
| after day 240, within 485 days | yes, if it shows good health | must show good health |
| later than that | not accepted | — |

## Boundary cases (hypothetical dates)

*Hypothetical inputs: SGLI coverage ended on 10 January 2025. Day 1 of the count is 11 January 2025.*

- Received **7 September 2025** — this is day 240, the last day. Accepted without health questions.
- Received **8 September 2025** — this is day 241, one day past the no-health window. Accepted only if the application shows good health.
- Received **6 November 2025** — day 300, within 485 days. Accepted only if the application shows good health.
- Received **25 May 2026** — day 500, beyond 485 days. Not accepted.

## Initial coverage

- **Ceiling.** Initial coverage cannot exceed the SGLI coverage held at separation.
- **Range and steps.** Coverage is chosen in multiples of $10,000, between $10,000 and $500,000.
- **Start.** Coverage begins when the first premium is received with the application.

*Hypothetical:* an applicant who held $300,000 of SGLI coverage at separation may choose initial coverage of, for example, $250,000 or $300,000, but not $310,000 (above the SGLI coverage held) and not $255,000 (not a multiple of $10,000).

## Basis questions

- *The applicant says SGLI ended later than the record shows. Which date counts?* The date SGLI coverage ended as recorded by the system for that applicant.
- *Is an application received exactly on day 240 inside the no-health window?* Yes. An application received on the last day qualifies.
- *Does coverage start on the date the application is approved?* Coverage begins when the first premium is received with the application.
